Package com.egradx.notification.auth

Class EgradxAuthRecipientDirectory

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.notification.auth.EgradxAuthRecipientDirectory
All Implemented Interfaces:
EgradxRecipientDirectory
public class EgradxAuthRecipientDirectory extends Object implements EgradxRecipientDirectory
Audiences for bulk sends, from egradx-auth: an organization's active members, or every active user. Paged by user id in the database's own order — see EgradxRecipientDirectory.page(com.egradx.notification.spi.EgradxRecipientDirectory.Audience, java.util.UUID, int) for why ids are never compared in Java here.

    • page

      public List<UUID> page(EgradxRecipientDirectory.Audience audience, UUID after, int limit)
      Description copied from interface: EgradxRecipientDirectory
      Ids in ascending order as the implementation orders them — any consistent order will do.

      The first page is asked for with after == null, not with a "lowest possible id": there is no id that is lowest in every ordering. PostgreSQL compares UUIDs as unsigned bytes, Java's UUID.compareTo as signed longs, so a sentinel of all zeros is first in one and lands mid-way in the other — and every id before it would be silently skipped. (That is not hypothetical: it is the bug this contract's first version had.)

      Specified by:
      page in interface EgradxRecipientDirectory
      Parameters:
      after - the last id of the previous page; null for the first page
      Returns:
      at most limit user ids after after, in the implementation's order
